correctness.rationale: Every force agrees with any proper extension of the current assignment, proving uniqueness when the process succeeds. If the assignment is incomplete, the first force requires lambda minus one distinct neighbour colours and introduces or uses the last colour. Different parts have disjoint final palettes. Thus a part with two or more final colours can never receive a force, and two empty monochromatic parts would prevent the first force. Conversely, if at most one part is empty and all multicoloured parts are full, an empty part fills first if present; all remaining vertices in seeded monochromatic parts then see every other colour. The falling factorial and Stirling product count ordered disjoint part palettes and within-part surjections; the subtraction in the correction removes exactly the already-counted total assignment. For the minimum, one can empty a monochromatic part and keep just one seed in every other monochromatic part. The extra colours can be assigned to the remaining split parts precisely when their number is at most the surplus and their aggregate capacities reach it. A smallest possible target part attains the degree cutoff: choose lambda-1 colour classes over the outside parts (at least one and at most their sizes per part), then use the remaining colour on the target. If the palette exceeds the cutoff the total-colouring term still applies, even when lambda>N.

originality.rationale: The cited chromatic and three-colour comparisons are not the complete coverage picture. Three distinct earlier indexed results jointly cover every admissible parameter: all excess palettes on two shores, one spare colour on r>=3 parts, and two or more spare colours on r>=3 parts. The proof structure, full coefficient enumerator and minimum in the last range match directly, and the other ranges match by specialization or elementary coefficient conversion. The unified statement leaves no distinct uncovered scientific result.
residual_risks: The coverage decision is a statement comparison with identifiable earlier corpus records, not a resolution of historical priority for the predecessors themselves.
